CRL.M.(BAIL) 339/2026 (for suspension of sentence)
2. The present application has been filed by the Appellant-Sunil Kumar under Section 430 read with Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (hereinafter, 'BNSS') seeking suspension of sentence and release on bail during the pendency of the present appeal.
3. The incident relating to the death of late Smt. Neelam, wife of Jaipal, is the subject matter of the present appeal.

On 9th October, 2011, the said unfortunate incident took place at House No. A-36,
Sanjay Colony, Bhati

The prosecution relies upon the Sunil Kumar vs State Of Nct Of Delhi on 7 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104514174/
1 dying declaration given by the deceased against her husband-Shri Jaipal, brother of her husband - Shri Rajpal, second brother of her husband- Shri. Sunil Kumar, as also the sister- in-law, i.e. sister of her husband- Smt. Rama Devi and father-in-law- Shri Babiya Ram @ Tota Ram.

sentences.text: 4. The Trial Court has convicted Jaipal, Rajpal, Babiya Ram @ Tota Ram and Sunil Kumar under Sections 302/498A of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

Vide order on sentence dated 19th April 2025,
the convicted persons have been awarded the sentence of life imprisonment along with fine.
The matter has also been referred to the District Legal Services Authority (South) for awarding compensation to the family of the deceased.
5. The submission on behalf of the Appellant is that there are inconsistencies in the dying declarations given by the deceased.
The deceased had, in fact, given a statement to the Sub-Divisional Magistrate (hereinafter, 'SDM'), which is exhibited as Ex.PW7/A, in which she had only named her husband.
However, after a couple of days, a second statement was given by the deceased being Ex. PW32/X.

In the said video, which was given after the statement to the SDM, the deceased had stated that she had been burnt by her husband, devar-Sunil i.e., the Appellant and nanand- Rama Devi and the father-in-law-Shri Babiya Ram @ Tota Ram was sitting outside and watching.
6. Ld. Counsel for the Appellant submits that in the statement given to the SDM i.e., Ex. PW7/A, no allegation was made against Appellant and she had only implicated her husband.
Ld. Counsel further submits that even in the statement of the eye-witnesses, the Appellant is not implicated at all and thus, This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 07/04/2026 at 21:38:53 he is entitled for suspension of sentence.
7.
Mr. Bahri, ld. APP has vehemently opposed the present application seeking suspension of sentence.
It is his case that the entire family has subjected the deceased to enormous cruelty and harassment.

The statement of the deceased i.e., Ex.PW32/X is consistent with her earlier statement as well that she was subjected to harassment due to demand for dowry and that all of the family members were involved in the incident as well.
8. Ld. APP further submits that the family made enormous efforts to get the dying declaration recorded and then exhibited and, therefore, sufficient credence ought to be given to the same.
9. Heard ld. Counsel for the parties.
At this stage, the Court is only considering the application for suspension of sentence filed by the Appellant.

10. The independent witness, i.e. the lady in the neighbourhood - PW-1, whose statements under Sections 161 and 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereinafter, 'CrPC') were recorded,
has not implicated the Appellant.
It is her testimony that she had seen the deceased in a burnt condition and, according to her, the Appellant was responsible to take her to the hospital.

According Sunil Kumar vs State Of Nct Of Delhi on 7 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104514174/
2 to PW-1, the Appellant had in fact broken the lock of the room to take the keys of the car to take the deceased to the hospital.

sentences.text: These statements are in fact consistent with the statements which PW-1 had given to the police at the time when the investigation was going on as well.

11. At this stage, in so far as the dying declarations are concerned, the initial dying declaration of the deceased was given to the SDM and in the same she merely alleges that the husband was suspecting that the child with whom she was pregnant did not belong to him and, therefore, he had poured kerosene on her and she had lit up herself.
In this statement, the deceased does This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 07/04/2026 at 21:38:53 not make any allegation or implicate the Appellant.

12. Even, in the final dying declaration which is relied upon by the prosecution i.e., Ex. PW 32/X, the same was recorded by a relative on a mobile phone and, therefore, the credibility of the same would be required to be gone into by the Court.
13. The Appellant himself is only 38 years of age.
He is married and has two children.
The Appellant being the devar of the deceased, the Court, at this stage, is inclined to suspend sentence of the Appellant.

14. Accordingly, sentence of the Appellant is suspended during the pendency of the present appeal,
subject to the following conditions:
i.

The Appellant shall be released upon furnishing a personal bond for a sum of Rs.25,000/-, with a surety of the like amount, to the satisfaction of the Trial Court/Link Court;
ii.

The Appellant shall intimate the concerned SHO, P.S. Fatehpur Beri, regarding his residential address where he would be residing upon release, and shall also inform the SHO regarding any change in his residential address;
iii.
The Appellant shall not, directly or indirectly, contact the family members of the complainant/deceased in any manner; v.

The Appellant shall report at the office of the concerned SHO, P.S. Fatehpur Beri, on the first Monday of every month at 11:00 a.m. and he shall be discharged by 12 noon, after recording his presence and completion of all the necessary formalities;
This is a digitally signed order.

The Appellant shall not indulge in any criminal activity and upon any such activity being discovered or indulged into, the present suspension of sentence shall automatically stand cancelled; vii.

The Appellant shall not leave the country without prior permission of this Court;
viii.
The Appellants shall appear before this Court as and when the matter is taken up for hearing.
15. It is made clear that this Court has not made any observations in respect of the other co-accused persons or discussed their role.
16. The application is disposed of in the above terms.
17. Copy of this order be sent to the concerned Jail Superintendent for necessary information and compliance.

19. List in due course.
